Repo: /home/lane/MythosMini — a 1,050,241-param byte-level (vocab 257) looped-shared-block transformer trained on fineweb-edu, benchmarked on WikiText-2 byte PPL, BLiMP, ARC-Easy against the Tiny-ML leaderboard (overall = mean of blimp, arc, normalized wiki score; efficiency = overall/log10(params+1) so PARAMETER GROWTH IS PENALIZED only logarithmically — doubling params costs ~5% efficiency but any overall gain counts fully). Current pipeline: procedural Dyck warmup -> 2B-token training (NAdamW, WSD schedule) -> 3-round recursive STM -> benchmark all checkpoints -> SLERP tournament -> SFT instruct phase -> instruct SLERP. Architecture: 4 prelude + 1 shared block looped 2-6x with per-loop LoRA + 4 coda, dim 96, RMSNorm/RoPE/SwiGLU, tied embeddings, DSA-style sparse attention (shared model-level lightning indexer, top-128 keys, 64 local window, FlexAttention short path, chunked long path, 1M max context), FP4 E2M1 QAT on all linears. Recent regression: moving the indexer from per-attention to one shared model-level indexer + detaching the indexer bias for prelude/coda blocks raised throughput 0.85->1.19 Mtok/s but the verification run scored 59.47 overall vs 60.40 before, AND its STM round 3 NaN-diverged (prior runs round 3 gave +0.57; NaN also seen once before with output-embedding centering). All-time best: 60.41 (recursive STM, commit accd37b). GPU: one RTX 5090 32GB, torch 2.10.0+cu128. Known: full-model torch.compile broken (inductor dtype bug + flex recompile issues), STM phase runs at only ~76 ktok/s vs training 1.19 Mtok/s. USER GOAL: push output quality as far as possible toward Gemma-class coherence (text in/text out) — ambition is the point; consider parameter growth, distillation, synthetic data, anything that fits one 5090.

Read /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/training/stm.py and src/mythosmini/benchmarks/*.py and src/mythosmini/merging/tournament.py. The STM phase runs at ~76 ktok/s while main training hits 1.19 Mtok/s — find out why (per-sample loss with reduction=none, fixed loops=4, micro 128 after OOM shrink, flex recompiles from varying batch shapes — note dynamo recompile limit 8 with dynamic=False compile of flex_attention, the final partial batch shape). Propose concrete speedups with exact code changes. Also check benchmark/tournament phases for waste. Target: STM phase at >=500 ktok/s.

51	def per_sample_loss(model: MythosMini, batch: Tensor, loops: int, dtype: torch.dtype) -> Tensor:
52	    device_type = batch.device.type
53	    with torch.autocast(device_type=device_type, dtype=dtype, enabled=dtype != torch.float32):
54	        logits = model(batch[:, :-1], loops=loops)
55	        vocab = logits.shape[-1]
56	        flat = functional.cross_entropy(
57	            logits.reshape(-1, vocab), batch[:, 1:].reshape(-1), reduction="none"

62	def select_survivors(previous: Tensor, current: Tensor, floor_quantile: float) -> Tensor:
63	    drops = previous - current
64	    if drops.numel() < 2:
65	        return torch.ones_like(current, dtype=torch.bool)
66	    threshold = drops.mean() + drops.std()
67	    floor = torch.quantile(current.float(), floor_quantile)
68	    mastered = (drops > threshold) & (current < floor)

35	    target_scores = log_probs.gather(-1, batch[:, 1:].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)

155	    arc_best = max(parents, key=lambda c: c.scores.arc)

168	def aggregate_score(

171	    arc_ref: tuple[float, float],
172	    wiki_log_ref: tuple[float, float],
173	) -> float:
174	    def normalize(val: float, ref: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
175	        if ref[1] == ref[0]:
176	            return 0.5
177	        return (val - ref[0]) / (ref[1] - ref[0])
178	
179	    blimp_n = normalize(scores.blimp, blimp_ref)
180	    arc_n = normalize(scores.arc, arc_ref)
181	    wiki_log = -math.log(max(scores.wiki_ppl, 1e-9))
182	    wiki_n = normalize(wiki_log, wiki_log_ref)

186	def run_tournament(

188	    evaluate: Evaluator,

191	    if not seeds:
192	        raise ValueError("tournament needs at least one seed candidate")
193	
194	    blimps = [s.scores.blimp for s in seeds]
195	    arcs = [s.scores.arc for s in seeds]
196	    wiki_logs = [-math.log(max(s.scores.wiki_ppl, 1e-9)) for s in seeds]
197	    b_ref = (min(blimps), max(blimps))
198	    a_ref = (min(arcs), max(arcs))
199	    w_ref = (min(wiki_logs), max(wiki_logs))
200	
201	    population = select_diverse(seeds, SLERP_TOP_K)
202	    best_overall = population[0]
203	    best_score = aggregate_score(best_overall.scores, b_ref, a_ref, w_ref)
204	    best_average = max(normalized_averages(population))
205	    stalled = 0
206	
207	    for generation in range(SLERP_MAX_GENERATIONS):
208	        if len(population) < 2:
209	            log(f"tournament stopped: single candidate after generation {generation}")
210	            break
211	        previous_best = category_best(population)
212	        children = build_generation(population, generation, evaluate)
213	        if not children:
214	            log(f"tournament stopped: no eligible pairs in generation {generation}")
215	            break
216	
217	        for child in children:
218	            score = aggregate_score(child.scores, b_ref, a_ref, w_ref)
219	            if score > best_score:
220	                best_score = score
221	                best_overall = child
222	
223	        if not any(improves_any_category(child.scores, previous_best) for child in children):
224	            log(f"tournament stopped: generation {generation} children worse in all categories")
225	            break
226	
227	        population = select_diverse(population + children, SLERP_TOP_K)
228	        current_best = max(normalized_averages(population))
229	        stalled = stalled + 1 if current_best <= best_average else 0
230	        best_average = max(best_average, current_best)
231	        log(f"generation {generation}: population {len(population)}, stalled {stalled}")
232	        if stalled >= STALL_GENERATIONS:
233	            log("tournament stopped: no improvement for three generations")
234	            break
235	    return best_overall

51	    batch, queries, keys = scores.shape
52	    query_positions = torch.arange(keys - queries, keys, device=scores.device).view(1, queries, 1)
53	    key_positions = torch.arange(keys, device=scores.device).view(1, 1, keys)
54	    causal = key_positions <= query_positions
55	    local = causal & (key_positions > query_positions - local_window)
56	    ranked = scores.masked_fill(~causal, float("-inf"))
57	    ranked = ranked + local.to(scores.dtype) * LOCAL_WINDOW_BONUS
58	    effective_k = min(top_k, keys)
59	    indices = ranked.topk(effective_k, dim=-1).indices
60	    selected = torch.zeros(batch, queries, keys, dtype=torch.bool, device=scores.device)
61	    selected = selected.scatter(-1, indices, True) & causal
62	    return indices, selected

245	            k.unsqueeze(2).expand(batch, heads, chunk_len, k.shape[2], head_dim), 3, expanded
246	        )

248	            v.unsqueeze(2).expand(batch, heads, chunk_len, v.shape[2], head_dim), 3, expanded
249	        )

301	class MythosMini(nn.Module):
302	    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int = 8) -> None:
303	        super().__init__()
304	        self.config = config
305	        self.max_loops = max_loops
306	        self.embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.dim)
307	        self.indexer = SparseIndexer(config)
308	        self.prelude = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.prelude_layers))
309	        self.shared = Block(config)
310	        self.loop_lora = LoopLora(config, max_loops)
311	        self.loop_embed = nn.Embedding(max_loops, config.dim)
312	        self.coda = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.coda_layers))
313	        self.final_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
314	        cos, sin = build_rope_cache(config)
315	        self.register_buffer("rope_cos", cos, persistent=False)
316	        self.register_buffer("rope_sin", sin, persistent=False)
317	
318	    def ensure_rope_length(self, seq_len: int) -> None:
319	        if seq_len > self.config.max_context_len:
320	            raise ValueError(
321	                f"sequence length {seq_len} exceeds max context {self.config.max_context_len}"
322	            )
323	        cached = cast(Tensor, self.rope_cos)
324	        if seq_len <= cached.shape[0]:
325	            return
326	        cos, sin = build_rope_cache(self.config, seq_len)
327	        self.rope_cos = cos.to(cached.device)
328	        self.rope_sin = sin.to(cached.device)
329	
330	    def forward(self, tokens: Tensor, loops: int | None = None) -> Tensor:
331	        loop_count = loops if loops is not None else self.config.shared_loops
332	        seq_len = tokens.shape[1]
333	        self.ensure_rope_length(seq_len)
334	        x = self.embed(tokens)
335	        device_type = tokens.device.type
336	        compute_dtype = (
337	            torch.get_autocast_dtype(device_type)
338	            if torch.is_autocast_enabled(device_type)
339	            else x.dtype
340	        )
341	        cos = cast(Tensor, self.rope_cos)[:seq_len].to(compute_dtype)
342	        sin = cast(Tensor, self.rope_sin)[:seq_len].to(compute_dtype)
343	        selection = self.indexer(x)
344	        frozen = selection.detached()
345	        for block in self.prelude:
346	            x = block(x, cos, sin, None, frozen)
347	        for loop_index in range(loop_count):
348	            clamped = min(loop_index, self.max_loops - 1)
349	            gated = x + self.loop_embed.weight[clamped]
350	            delta = self.loop_lora(gated, loop_index)
351	            x = self.shared(gated, cos, sin, delta, selection)
352	        for block in self.coda:
353	            x = block(x, cos, sin, None, frozen)
354	        x = self.final_norm(x)
355	        return functional.linear(x, self.embed.weight)

11	def quantize_fp4(weight: Tensor, block: int = FP4_BLOCK) -> Tensor:
12	    original_shape = weight.shape
13	    flat = weight.reshape(-1)
14	    pad = (-flat.shape[0]) % block
15	    if pad:
16	        flat = functional.pad(flat, (0, pad))
17	    blocks = flat.reshape(-1, block)
18	    scales = blocks.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True) / FP4_MAX
19	    scales = scales.clamp_min(SCALE_EPS)
20	    normalized = blocks / scales
21	    levels = torch.tensor(FP4_LEVELS, dtype=normalized.dtype, device=normalized.device)
22	    midpoints = (levels[:-1] + levels[1:]) / 2
23	    nearest = levels[torch.bucketize(normalized.abs(), midpoints)]
24	    quantized = nearest * normalized.sign() * scales
25	    return quantized.reshape(-1)[: weight.numel()].reshape(original_shape)

findings.title: STM root cause: trailing partial micro-batches blow the dynamo recompile limit on flex_attention -> permanent eager fallback (measured 36 ktok/s vs 1,339 ktok/s fixed-shape). Fix: pad every micro-batch to a constant shape
findings.detail: In /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/training/stm.py `stm_epoch`, each epoch ends with a partial batch of size `indices.shape[0] % micro_batch`, and the pool shrinks every epoch, so every epoch produces a NEW batch shape. flex_attention is compiled with dynamic=False in /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/model/transformer.py `compiled_flex_attention`, and the guard fails on the `selected` closure tensor's batch dim (verified: 'tensor score_mod.__closure__[0].cell_contents size mismatch at index 0'). After 8 shapes dynamo stops compiling; eager flex materializes (B,H,512,512) score tensors for all 12 block-calls' backward — this is also what caused the OOM that shrank 256->128, and the new 128 bulk shape then arrived AFTER the limit, so entire epochs run eager. Fix in `stm_epoch`: pad the trailing batch by wrap-around and mask it out of the loss: replace the loop body with `position = indices[start : start + micro_batch]; count = position.shape[0]; if count < micro_batch: filler = indices[torch.arange(micro_batch - count, device=indices.device) % indices.shape[0]]; position = torch.cat([position, filler])` then `batch = pool[position]`, `sample_losses = per_sample_loss(...)`, `torch.autograd.backward(sample_losses[:count].mean())`, `losses[start : start + count] = sample_losses[:count].detach()`, `start += count`. Batch shape is then constant (micro_batch, 512) for the whole 3-round run (1-2 compiled graphs total). per_sample_loss reduction=none and fixed loops=4 are NOT the problem (probe used both and hit 1.34 Mtok/s).
findings.expected_gain: STM phase 76 ktok/s -> ~1,300 ktok/s (17x; measured 1,339 ktok/s fixed-shape fwd+bwd at micro 128 on the 5090), far above the 500 ktok/s target. Also removes the eager-flex memory spike that triggered the 256->128 OOM, so micro 256 should hold (~2x more tokens/step on top).
findings.risk: Low. Padded rows are excluded from the loss mean so gradients are identical; one extra wasted partial-batch forward per epoch (<0.3% compute). Edge case: late rounds where active pool < micro_batch is handled by the modulo filler. Update tests/test_stm.py for the new trailing-batch bookkeeping.

findings.title: Raise torch._dynamo recompile limit before compiling flex_attention so one-off shapes (autotune probes) can never poison the cache
findings.detail: In /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/model/transformer.py `compiled_flex_attention()`, before `torch.compile(flex_attention, dynamic=False)` add: `torch._dynamo.config.recompile_limit = 64` (alias `cache_size_limit`; default is 8, confirmed on torch 2.10.0+cu128). This matters because the same process runs autotune_batch_size (/home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/hardware/autotune.py) which probes batch sizes 8,16,32,64,128,256,... — each probe consumes a recompile slot before training/eval even starts — plus training shape, STM shape, eval autotune probes, and eval buckets. With limit 8, the budget is exhausted almost immediately; with 64 every recurring shape gets compiled once and stays fast (verified: previously-compiled shapes still serve at 1,317 ktok/s after the limit is hit — the damage is only to shapes that arrive after).
findings.expected_gain: Belt-and-braces for findings 1 and 3: guarantees the steady-state shapes are compiled, not eager. Without it, the ~7 autotune probe shapes alone nearly exhaust the limit. Costs only extra one-time compile latency (~10-30 s per shape, bounded by the small bucket count).
findings.risk: Very low. Only increases compile cache size. Do NOT switch to dynamic=True instead — flex + dynamic shapes is the known-broken recompile path on this setup; fixed shapes + bigger cache is the reliable combination.

findings.title: Benchmark scorer: bucket sequence lengths to multiples of 64 and fix the batch dimension (measured eval: 53 ktok/s ragged vs 3,947 ktok/s compiled)
findings.detail: /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/benchmarks/scorer.py `batch_log_likelihoods` pads each chunk to that chunk's exact max_len, so BLiMP (67 subtasks x 200 sentences) and ARC (500 x ~4 choices) generate dozens of distinct (batch, seq) shapes — all eager after the limit. Fix: (a) pass `batch_size` into `batch_log_likelihoods` and allocate `padded = torch.zeros(batch_size, max_len, ...)` (dummy zero rows for the trailing chunk; their scores are simply not read — the existing per-row `(tokens, continuation_len)` extraction already ignores them); (b) round seq up: `max_len = min(model.config.max_seq_len, ((raw_max + 63) // 64) * 64)`. Since rows are already sorted by length descending, this yields at most 8 seq buckets x 1 batch shape. Apply the same trailing-batch padding to /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/benchmarks/wikitext.py `byte_perplexity` (1023 rows -> final partial batch): pad the last batch to `batch_size` rows and switch to `cross_entropy(..., reduction='none')` summed over only the real rows.
findings.expected_gain: Eval forward throughput 53 -> ~2,000-3,900 ktok/s once the <=10 shapes are warm (measured fixed-shape compiled eval at 3,947 ktok/s; bucketed shapes hit 507 ktok/s even in the degraded eager regime). Each candidate eval is ~2.5-3M tokens (wikitext 0.5M + blimp ~1M + arc ~1M); the tournament runs up to ~75 evals per generation x up to 10 generations, so this turns the benchmark+tournament phases from hours into minutes. Bucket padding overhead ~1.3x compute, dwarfed by the speedup.
findings.risk: Low. Zero-padding rows/columns changes no real-row logits (causal attention; scores read only from real positions). Verify BLiMP/ARC/wiki numbers match pre-change on one checkpoint to ~1e-3 before trusting tournament results, since the sparse indexer top-k could in principle select padding keys — it cannot affect real rows (per-row independence) but padded key columns DO enter each real row's top-128 candidate set via the (B,Q,K) score matrix; padding only extends K for rows that are themselves padding when seq is bucketed per-chunk-max... since bucketing extends seq beyond some rows' lengths, real rows now see extra zero-token keys as eligible top-k candidates. Mitigation if scores drift: keep per-chunk exact max_len semantics by masking padded key positions to -inf in the indexer scores, or accept the (tiny, ReLU-gated) difference after verifying parity.

findings.title: Tournament re-evaluates identical SLERP merges every generation — make the dedup memo persistent across generations
findings.detail: /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/merging/tournament.py `build_generation` creates a fresh `seen` set per call, and `merge_key` is based on parent names + t. Because `select_diverse` keeps most parents across generations, the same (parentA, parentB, t) merges are re-SLERPed AND re-benchmarked in every generation (up to 15 pairs x 5 t-values = 75 evals/gen, largely repeats after gen 0). Fix: in `run_tournament` create `evaluated: dict[tuple[str, str, int], MergeCandidate] = {}` and pass it into `build_generation`; in `add_child`, `key = merge_key(a, b, t); cached = evaluated.get(key);` if cached, `children.append(cached)` (no eval) else build, eval, store. Memoize `build_centroid_merge` the same way keyed by the three parent names. Appending the cached candidate keeps `improves_any_category`/`select_diverse` semantics intact (name-keyed dedup in select_diverse already collapses duplicates).
findings.expected_gain: Eliminates 50-80% of merge evaluations in generations >= 1 (only pairs involving newly-admitted children are genuinely new). Combined with finding 3 this makes the SLERP phase nearly free; on its own it roughly halves tournament wall time.
findings.risk: Very low. Pure caching; scores are deterministic for a given state dict. Slight behavior note: a cached candidate retains its original genN name, which only affects log labels.

findings.title: Reuse one resident GPU model across all benchmark/tournament evaluations
findings.detail: /home/lane/MythosMini/train.py `benchmark_state_dict` constructs `MythosMini(model_config).to(info.device)` for every candidate (every checkpoint, every merge child, every SFT candidate). Construct the model once in `benchmark_phase` (the existing `reference` model works) and thread it through to `benchmark_state_dict`/the `evaluate` closures in `slerp_phase` and `sft_phase`, replacing construction with `model.load_state_dict(state)` (CPU->GPU copy of ~1M params). Also wrap eval in `torch.inference_mode()` in scorer.py/wikitext.py instead of no_grad for a small allocator win.
findings.expected_gain: Saves ~0.5-1 s of module init + allocator churn per candidate (hundreds of candidates per run -> minutes), and removes repeated CUDA allocations that fragment memory during long tournaments. Small but trivial to implement alongside finding 3.
findings.risk: Very low. load_state_dict fully overwrites parameters and rope buffers are non-persistent/shape-stable at 512; ensure model.eval() is set once.

findings.title: STM pool stored as int64 on GPU wastes 384 MB; store int32 and widen per batch (more headroom to keep micro 256)
findings.detail: /home/lane/MythosMini/src/mythosmini/training/stm.py `load_sample_pool` does `np.asarray(memmap[...], dtype=np.int64)` -> 64M tokens x 8 B = 512 MB resident on the 5090. Change to `dtype=np.int32` (vocab 257 fits easily) and in `stm_epoch` use `batch = pool[position].long()` (the .long() on a (256,513) slice is negligible). Saves 256 MB; combined with finding 1 removing the eager-flex memory spikes, micro_batch should settle at the full 256 instead of 128. Optionally also autotune the STM micro batch with the same `autotune_batch_size` harness (using a fixed loops=4 fwd+bwd probe) instead of the hardcoded 256, and add a non-finite guard in `stm_epoch` (`if not torch.isfinite(sample_losses).all(): skip optimizer.step()`) so a single bad batch cannot NaN the whole round-3 model as happened in the verification run.
findings.expected_gain: 256 MB VRAM freed; keeps micro 256 (2x tokens/step vs the post-OOM 128). The NaN guard protects the +0.5-ish overall points that round 3 historically contributes from being lost to divergence.
findings.risk: Low. int32->long conversion is exact. The NaN guard changes training semantics only on already-divergent steps; log skipped steps so divergence is visible rather than silent.
